Settle: if the ON OVERFLOW path must be witnessed per rule, this probe is the 2002 witness; otherwise UPHELD.

In 2002 a new interface instance is created whenever 'a parameterized interface is specified in the REPOSITORY paragraph'; in 2023 only when it is 'specified as the parameterized interface in an EXPANDS phrase'. 2023 GR7 also adds that a USING-described interface may be specified only in the REPOSITORY paragraph. cases.reason: In 2002, data-name-1/data-name-2 is a user-defined word 'including qualification and subscription if needed' (5.1.3), and a table element reference shall be subscripted (8.4.1.2.2 SR5). So RECORD KEY IS K(2), for K in an OCCURS, is legal 2002, and 2002 SR1 only adds 'may be qualified'. 2023 SR1 says data-name-1 and data-name-2 'shall not be subject to any OCCURS clauses'. The 2014 Annex E.2 item 25 says this restriction was added after 2002, which allowed subscripting by default. The reader's premise that the 2002 data-name admits no subscript is wrong. GR3 governs the 2002 subscripted key, and the 2023 verdict says nothing about it. Probe: both --std 2002 and --std 2023 reject RECORD KEY IS K(2) (COBOL2024, citing §2023:8.4.2.2.2), so the compiler at 2002 rejects legal 2002 source.

refute.notes: The fifth cause: 2002 lets data-name-n in a general format be subscripted by default (§2002:5.1.3; §2014:E.2 item 25 says so and says 2014 added the bans). 2023 forbids OCCURS for FILE STATUS, RECORD KEY, ALTERNATE RECORD KEY and RELATIVE KEY, and subscripts for key-level COLLATING SEQUENCE. Any word-identical rule on those clauses, or on the formats that hold them, is wider in 2002. The pinned compiler rejects these subscripts at --std 2002 with 2023 citations (COBOL2024), so it rejects legal 2002 source. Sweep the other 500 KEPT candidates for the same clauses and for 2023's other 'not subject to any OCCURS' rules (e.g. 13.18 at 2023 lines 16140, 17002, 18918, 19064, 25112, 27965, 28182).
